title: A one-bit memory
description:
Simulate an SR latch made from two NOR gates and show that it remembers.

```
S R | Q
1 0 | 1   set
0 0 | 1   remembers
0 1 | 0   reset
0 0 | 0   remembers
```
hints: `q = nor(r, q_bar)` and `q_bar = nor(s, q)`; repeat until neither changes (lesson 4.03).
For the register, a latch only gets `S = data and write` and `R = (not data) and write`.
requirements: `nor(a, b)` and a latch with two outputs `q` and `q_bar` that feed back into each other.
After each input change, update the gates a few times until the outputs stop changing.
Then build a 4-bit register from four latches with a shared "write" signal.
stretch: Show what happens with S = 1 and R = 1, and why real circuits avoid it.
